{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea 2 in using_call.md (2026-10-01), joined with the open question in fact:a-cli-call-in-a-pointer-folder-mints-a-fresh-local-store-2026-10-01, measured the same day. They are one question: where does a one-shot call go when the design is not simply a free local store?

THE IDEAS:
(a) Anthony: "`--call` joins a running shared daemon. When the graph is held by a `--serve-shared` daemon, route the call through it (the same proxy `--shared` uses) instead of refusing writes. VS Code and Claude Code could then work the same design at once." He calls it "the biggest functional gap" (limitation 3).
(b) From the pointer defect: in a folder whose `.reflow2.toml` names a hosted design, forward the call to that server, as the stdio client path already does.
(c) Or refuse there, naming the pointer's address.
(d) Or open the store only when it already exists.

WHAT IS CHEAP OR NOT: (c) and (d) are small, and either closes the stray-store hazard. (a) and (b) give one door that always reaches the real design. Through a daemon, writes would also get its write-through export, which narrows dec:idea-a-writing-call-exports-afterwards to the case with no daemon running. But (a) and (b) bring in the proxy path, with its known 2026-07-28 discovery issue (fact:through-the-shared-proxy-a-2026-07-28-server-discover-is-answered-as-an-unreachable-server-2026-09-26), and for (b) the remote client's credentials.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a build script that silently writes into someone's live session may not be what a build wants.
